entries.raw:
{gb} Ross Walker:

*BURNHAM SAYS HE'LL USE 'ANY FLEXIBILITY' WITHIN UK FISCAL RULES.
Not exactly sure what that means.
There was a modest amount of headroom on the OBR's March estimates for the main 'fiscal mandate' (~£24bn).
Presumably he'd want to retain some headroom (at least £5bn, maybe closer to £10bn).
I suspect the bigger risks here are around the 'supplementary target' (for public debt as a % of GDP to be falling by 2029-30 FY) - e.g., 'Flexibility' here might entail simply changing the definition of 'debt' and claim the debt rule is being met [if an employer National Insurance rise isn't a National Insurance rise in this Orwellian world, then I don't think this is beyond the realms of possibility].
